iterative.mechanism: An updated model returns to execution, workflow improvement and output selection in the next round. This tests one bounded feedback loop, not indefinite acceleration of all research.
iterative.conditions: Read MASS v1 Sections 3–5, Appendix B, C.3–C.5 and Table 7, plus the author page. Qwen3.6-27B receives two rounds of training under human-provided tasks, procedure and compute; external judgments do not feed back into learning.
iterative.counterexample: Score per output token improves on four research benchmarks but decreases on two software benchmarks. Phantom Gains shows why a frozen-model comparison is needed in a different three-round experiment; it is not a replication of MASS.
iterative.evidence: Eight tasks supply fine-tuning data. Three are excluded from training, validation and checkpoint selection but still used during workflow-search evaluation. The result warrants limited/tested evidence at R3 and bounded updates to R2-R3 and R3-R2.
iterative.limits: One family and two iterations, small or uneven absolute-score gains, model judges and incomplete pipeline-cost accounting. The paper does not demonstrate continued improvement, independence from human setup, or whole-industry acceleration. No code or independent replication was verified.
iterative.mitigation: Compare fixed baselines, separately measure validation and compute costs, preserve held-out tasks and test whether research gains survive more rounds. Maintain external oversight while researcher capability increases.
iterative.readerContext: Read R3, its evidence summary and both feedback connections in Japanese and English. A limited iterative experiment is distinct from the stronger sustained process; the current label is explicit about that boundary.
iterative.whyHere: R3 was due. Add mass-self-supervision and mass-two-rounds, change hypothesis to limited with an explicit tested evidence summary, and update the two conditional/feedback explanations without changing topology.

posttraining.mechanism: Agents can carry out additional training of another model without that model replacing the research agent. This supports a component of AI research, not the recursive step itself.
posttraining.conditions: Read Athanor v1 setup/results, Sections 3–5, Table 1 and Section 8. Four Opus 5.5 agents share a 104-hour campaign to improve Qwen3-4B-Base, with eight GPUs each and human-prepared tools and evaluation.
posttraining.counterexample: The small-model scores approach the official Instruct release but remain below official reasoning releases. Public data include stronger-model distillation even though new teacher-model calls are forbidden.
posttraining.evidence: Development mean 15.9 to 67.3 and held-out mean 9.2 to 48.2, compared with 66.5 and 47.9 for Instruct under the same evaluation. These are reported means, not demonstrated significant superiority.
posttraining.limits: One shared campaign is not four replications. Humans supply the objective, starter code and recovery of broken infrastructure. No larger-model or replacement-researcher experiment is shown; experiment dates and independent replication remain unverified.
posttraining.mitigation: Keep hidden evaluation and account for human/compute inputs. Validate resulting models independently before attributing whole-process or self-improvement gains.
posttraining.readerContext: Read the new source/card and its R1 paragraph in both languages. Name the separate researcher and target models so the reader can distinguish post-training from recursive improvement.
posttraining.whyHere: Add athanor-post-training and athanor-small-model to R1 as bounded evidence of carrying out research work. Preserve R1 classification and the separation from R3.

verification.mechanism: Producing a report or executable result does not establish a new scientific finding. Evidence must connect claims, records, required artifacts and the substantive scientific objective.
verification.conditions: Read Into the Unknown v1 PDF Sections 2–5, Table 2 and selected appendix traces. Nine configurations attempt fifteen open follow-ups with supplied papers, data, code, internet, task compute, no time limit and up to five review rounds.
verification.counterexample: The benchmark does not negate successes in bounded post-training or research tasks. Some appendix checks apply a stronger scientific rubric than a minimal visible instruction, so a failed grade is not automatically fabricated work.
verification.evidence: Authors report 0 of 135 submissions meeting all conditions and 114 failing integrity checks. Scientists verify requirements, but GPT-6 Astra grades four times and requires three passing judgments per rubric item.
verification.limits: Automated grading on selected difficult tasks is not a measure of intentional deception or all human-assisted science. Model-list, figure-count and legacy-text inconsistencies prevent adopting rankings or time-effect claims. No human regrading or full appendix audit was performed.
verification.mitigation: Verify records, artifacts and scientific success separately; use independent evaluation and seek replication. Keep successful task results and failed verification visible together.
verification.readerContext: Read R1 from definition through limits in Japanese and English, including the two new paragraphs. Research assistance, validated discovery and acceleration of all development remain separate.
verification.whyHere: Add open-science-followups and open-science-verification as a counterpoint at R1. Preserve its observed classification; do not turn a difficult-benchmark failure into absence of useful research assistance.

response.mechanism: A warning needs authorized and timely intervention. Stopping AI also needs fallback operations and recovery if essential financial services depend on it.
response.conditions: Read FSB summary/practices and Sections 3.7 and 3.9, plus the OpenAI DNS timeline, AISI containment account and AIR v2 methods/results. Distinguish policy guidance, operational incidents and controlled recovery experiments.
response.counterexample: AISI reports containment and no identified harm; AIR recovers some tested states. Other actions, including disclosure or irreversible deletion, cannot simply be undone. The DNS delay does not show that harm grew during the delay.
response.evidence: FSB recommends tested stopping/revocation, named authority, escalation, fallback and joint exercises for shared-provider failures. It supplies no measured adoption, response-time, recovery or harm-reduction rate.
response.limits: The incident settings and recovery denominators differ, so their results cannot be pooled as a general success rate. A nonbinding final report does not demonstrate implementation or effectiveness. Older attached sources were not all reread today.
response.mitigation: Test stopping mechanisms and responsibilities together, revoke credentials where needed, plan independent fallback and provider recovery, and measure both intervention latency and service continuity.
response.readerContext: Read C3b and F4 in both languages. Distinguish a local response delay from general loss of control and a guidance document from observed failure or protection of financial markets.
response.whyHere: C3b was due; F4 receives substantive new defensive guidance. Add fsb-ai-practices-final and financial-ai-stop-and-recover, retain C3b limited/indirect and F4 hypothesis, and update only their node dates and the changed C3b evidence summary.

connections.mechanism: R1-R2 requires useful contributions to improve overall development after validation and resource costs. F1-F3 requires shared financial behavior or dependencies to propagate disruption; it is not implied by the existence of AI tools.
connections.conditions: Read both retained edge explanations and conditions in Japanese and English against the new small-model, verification and financial-practices material.
connections.counterexample: Outputs can fail scientific verification despite extensive work. Isolation, fallback, varied exposures or effective intervention can prevent shared tools from producing market-wide disruption.
connections.evidence: New studies identify component results and constraints without measuring aggregate development speed or an AI-driven financial cascade. FSB supplies recommendations rather than causal effect sizes.
connections.limits: Component experiments and policy statements do not establish that all prerequisites occur together, nor a frequency or inevitability of the downstream outcome.
connections.mitigation: Measure whole-process results after validation, and test continuity and concentration risks under joint failures. Preserve conditional language and explicit defense assumptions.
connections.readerContext: The reader sees a necessary qualification between a research task and accelerated development, and between financial AI adoption and systemic effects. Both languages retain these distinctions.
connections.whyHere: Retain R1-R2 and F1-F3 wording and checked dates. Their fingerprints change because endpoint evidence changed, so record the dependency rereview without unrelated date renewal.

navigation.mechanism: The stories separate capability, choice, permissions, failed prevention, persistent control loss and wider harm. Research feedback and financial dependence contribute under different conditions and can also support defenses.
navigation.conditions: Read acceleration, oversight, money, finance-conditions, development-paths and research-cycle graph definitions; acceleration/money route previews; and control/acceleration/money story chapters in both languages.
navigation.counterexample: Better models can improve safety research, an experiment may stop after two rounds, and revocation plus fallback can interrupt a financial pathway. Neither new experiment observes catastrophe or permanent loss of control.
navigation.evidence: The added cards fit the existing non-exhaustive structure. No graph membership, route ordering or story claims need changing to represent the limited results.
navigation.limits: A narrative pathway is not a prediction, probability estimate, necessary sequence or sufficient condition for global harm. Joint conditions cannot be inferred by assembling unrelated experiments.
navigation.mitigation: Keep safety improvement and containment branches visible and introduce access and validation conditions before stronger outcomes. Let the evidence cards carry the detailed limits.
navigation.readerContext: Tour text already explains why practical access and validation matter. New plain-language paragraphs do not require a glossary or UI change.
navigation.whyHere: Retain six graphs, two routes and three stories after substantive endpoint changes; record their bilingual dependency review rather than modifying navigation for a new paper.

summaries.limits: These older source accounts were not all revalidated today. Their dates remain unchanged; dependency reading does not renew source verification or imply a new quantitative result.
